newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil adds acreage in Gulf of Mexico, Australia.
newsitem.headline: Statoil adds acreage in Gulf of Mexico, Australia.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday that it had secured interests in two new exploration blocks in the Gulf of Mexico and acreage on the Australian continental shelf.
Statoil and operator Conoco Inc acquired 50 percent each in blocks 810 and 766 in the Alaminos Canyon area off Texas after bidding for seven blocks.
Conoco is a unit of DuPont Co.
Both holdings are in about 2,000 metres of water close to the U.S.-Mexican boundary line.
Statoil said a number of large structures had been identified in the region, but none had been drilled so far. The two blocks cover much of one such structure, it said.

Egil Endresen of Statoil's international exploration and production unit said Statoil and Conoco planned to map the area in great detail through seismic surveys. Drilling could begin in two to three years.
"This is a challenging part of the world, and we are able to drill in such water depths. We also have technology to tackle possible developments there," Endresen said.

Statoil has also gained a 25 percent stake in Australian block 95-18, 400 km northwest of Darwin. Operator Mobil Corp and Royal Dutch/Shell also hold 25 percent each, the remining partners being Hardy Oil & Gas Plc with 13 percent and Mitsubishi with 12 percent.
The consortium will be based in Darwin and hopes to find gas reserves that could form the basis for a plant to produce liquefied natural gas, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
The block lies in an area designated as Zone of Cooperation by the Australian and Indonesian authorities. The venture includes sharing revenues from operations in the area.
